title: Rapid Ops seller notes and lane cues (draft)
body:
Objective: give sellers a 3–5 minute tactical script + lane-specific cues to run operational/technical pilot conversations. Keep it noise-free: one-line value, three proof points, one low-risk pilot ask, and fallback verbatim for objections.

Structure:
- TL;DR one-liner (ops-flavored)
- Lane cues: Integration Architect / Platform Engineer / Product Manager / Procurement / Executive
- Quick demo script (3 steps)
- Canary & fallback checklist (pilot-safe)
- Pricing anchor + reserved vs hosted decision note
- Post-call email template + next-step ask
- Open questions to capture and slingshot to SE/solutions team

----
TL;DR (ops-flavored):
"Redwood lets your teams run production-grade LLM features with predictable latency and cost by giving you a single runtime that ships across Hosted API, Reserved GPU pools, or Private VPCs — and a set of fast fallback rules so customer-facing features stay up during load or upgrades."

Top 3 proof points to cite quickly:
1) Predictable SLOs: configurable latency and throughput targets per-model + automated fallbacks to compatible variants.
2) Unit economics control: batching + prefix caching + quantization profiles reduce per-token cost 2–6x vs naive hosting on GPU.
3) Easy pilot modes: start on Hosted API for integration, escalate to Reserved Pools for throughput guarantees, or stump into Private VPC for compliance — same API & telemetry.

Lane cues (short scripts and technical hooks):
- Integration Architect (what to ask / say):
  - Opening: "What's your current request/response latency target and 99th p95 behavior during peak?"
  - Hook: "We can show a 10–30% latency drop by moving to continuous batching and kernel selection tuned to your sequence length distribution."
  - Proof: mention prefix/KV cache and demo synthetic load showing tail latency.
  - Red flag: heavy short chat traffic with lots of short-turn conversations (point to cache strategy).
  - Quick ask: Give me a sample of 1k requests so we can replay and show a perf/cost delta in 48 hours.

- Platform Engineer / SRE (what to ask / say):
  - Opening: "Who owns incident playbooks for ML infra? How do you currently handle model fallbacks during overload?"
  - Hook: "Redwood exposes routing policies and canary fallbacks as config; no code changes to apps — route by latency or cost tier."
  - Proof: show routing policy UI screenshot + trace of automatic fallback to quantized variant without user-visible error.
  - Red flag: strict network egress rules or air-gapped environments (point to Private deployment pack).
  - Quick ask: Can we get a short architecture diagram or a runbook excerpt so we can propose a fallback plan?

- Product Manager (what to ask / say):
  - Opening: "What's the worst outcome for users when LLM calls slow or spike in cost?"
  - Hook: "We let you set SLOs per-route and measure token-level cost in the console so you can trade off precision vs economics without guesswork."
  - Proof: demo per-route cost dashboard and a quality-monitoring alert tied to a prompt set.
  - Quick ask: Can you share 2–3 canonical prompts so we can run a quality baseline within 72 hours?

- Procurement / Legal (what to ask / say):
  - Opening: "What controls do you need for data residency and key management?"
  - Hook: "We offer Private VPC with KMS/HSM integration and audited logs; reserved contracts available for committed capacity."
  - Proof: link to a short compliance checklist + example MSA bullet points.
  - Quick ask: Request a basic security questionnaire (we'll fill the first pass in 48 hours).

- Executive / Line-of-Business (what to ask / say):
  - Opening: "What is the business outcome we can measure from a successful pilot (reduction in manual work, conversion lift, retention)?"
  - Hook: "Typical pilots show clear unit-cost improvements and reliability gains that scale with traffic; reserved pools give cost predictability for scale."
  - Proof: quick case reference (anonymized) and % improvements.
  - Quick ask: 2-week technical pilot with a defined success metric and a decision checkpoint.

Quick 3-step demo script (3–5 minutes live):
1) App flow: show a minimal request from client -> Redwood API -> response. Emphasize same API across modes. (45s)
2) Console: open per-route cost & latency dashboard, toggle a fallback policy (canary, quantized variant). (90s)
3) Show a short trace: request shadowing and KV cache hit rate improvement; highlight token cost delta on a small sample. (60s)

Canary & fallback checklist (pilot-safe, seller handed to SE):
- Pre-call: confirm sample workload (100–1k requests) and typical sequence lengths.
- Pilot config: set SLO, enable prefix/KV caching, propose two model variants (high-quality, quantized fallback).
- Canary steps: deploy a 5–10% canary of traffic for 24h, measure p95 and token cost.
- Fallback policy: automated route to quantized model after sustained latency > threshold, with alert to SRE.
- Success metric: maintain 95% of requests under target latency and <x% cost uplift vs baseline.

Pricing anchor + reserved vs hosted decision note (seller script):
- Start by anchoring on speed to value: "Hosted API lets you unblock integration in <1 day."
- When asked about unit cost: "For steady-state production, reserved pools typically yield 20–50% lower per-token cost depending on batchability and sequence lengths."
- If they ask for hard numbers: offer to run a 72-hr sample replay and return an estimated per-1k token unit cost with assumptions.

Buyer objections + fallback lines (verbatim):
- "We host our own models already" -> "Totally valid. Teams often start with our runtime to get predictable SLOs and rollback/fallback policies without refactoring app logic; we can run a side-by-side on your sample workload in 48–72 hours."
- "Security / data residency concerns" -> "We have a Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) and integrate with KMS/HSM; we’ll start with a compliance Q&A and map gaps."
- "Costs look high" -> "Let's run a cost-replay with your real requests and show where batching, cache, and quantization could reduce costs — we typically find savings quickly."

Post-call email template (send within 24h):
Subject: Redwood pilot next steps + quick artifacts
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the time today — summary and next steps below:
- Pilot scope: 2-week integration on Hosted API with X sample prompts and a 5% canary, OR reserved pool estimate if you prefer.
- Requests we need: sample workload (100–1k requests), infra diagram (network & egress rules), compliance questionnaire if needed.
- Proposed milestone: perf & cost baseline (72h) -> canary (week 2) -> decision checkpoint.
I'll loop in Mateo (SE) to schedule the baseline run.
Best,
Priya

Open questions to capture and route to SE after the call: (capture verbatim from prospect)
- Are there any non-standard auth or proxy layers between app and internet?
- Typical sequence length distribution (tokens) by endpoint?
- Expected throughput during peak minute/hour?
- Procurement timeline for reserved capacity (if interested)?

Prep checklist for the seller before call:
- Bring a single slide: 1-line value + 3 proof bullets + pilot ask.
- Have 2 quick live screenshots in drive: console-cost, routing-policy.
- Know the quick numbers: typical hosted API onboarding (same-day), reserved commit lead times (2–4 weeks), expected unit cost split drivers (batchability, cache hit rate, quantization).

Notes for SE handoff: export workload sample, include recorded demo snippet, attach any compliance docs requested, and align on canary thresholds.

Measurements to watch during pilot (what to log & report):
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route; tokens per response; average batch size; cache hit rate; per-route token cost.

Collect these for the pilot wrap: one-paragraph outcome + a 3-line decision recommendation (scale reserved / continue hosted / private deploy).

One-liners for quick wins:
- "Stop guessing token costs — measure them route-by-route."
- "Protect user experience with automated fallbacks, not brittle custom code."
- "Same API across Hosted, Reserved, and Private — reduce ops friction."

Appendix (helpful links and artifacts to attach quickly):
- Short compliance checklist (one-pager)
- Example canary playbook (developer-friendly)
- Sample workload replay guide + script

Editor notes / open items (internal):
- Add anonymized customer percent improvements after next case wins.
- Build quick demo video (90s) that shows toggling fallback policy and trace.
- Get up-to-date reserved pricing ranges to replace placeholders in final draft.

End of draft.
